product_from_film: Servo7 offers robots intended to fit existing industrial workflows, illustrated by picking and packing products.
explains_well: A simple conveyor-and-box diagram makes the repetitive task clear before robot handling footage appears.
unclear: The film does not show installation or adaptation in the pictured existing conveyor workflow.
scenario: Replace manual conveyor pick-and-pack work without redesigning the facility.
product_clear_basis: The adaptive-robot claim at 22s becomes a specific conveyor pick-and-pack task at 26s.

categories.finding: Cost/setup problem → adaptive robots → packing example → customer/team context → invitation.
Two founders appear beneath oversized cost text; the amount is changing in samples rather than a stable quoted price.
Industrial logistics, assembly and manufacturing teams are addressed; conveyor packing makes the task clear at 26s.
Illustrated products change position along/away from the conveyor; text and audience cards appear over presenters. Exact motion paths and robot cycle are unresolved at 1fps.
The conveyor diagram bridges the abstract setup problem to close robot footage, but they are not visibly the same installed workstation.
Warm workshop footage contrasts with dark factories and a restrained gray technical illustration.
Large words emphasize cost and inefficiency; the diagram explains packing. Team-experience labels should not be confused with demonstrated product use.
ASR supports the problem and packing explanation; several technical phrases are corrected only where visible text supports them. Audio delivery is unknown.

Effects and their sources are unverified.

categories.finding: Text and conveyor/box diagram carry the broad proposition; exact adaptation mechanism is not visible.
The diagram isolates three products and a box, while big text focuses the interview’s argument.
About 15s explain the simple packing scenario; the final 19s add team background, industries and contact. Setup proof is missing.
The no-redesign promise receives a packing concept and hardware footage, but no before/after installation evidence.
Cost/friction framing gives way to an apparently simple task and capable team; response is unmeasured.
Packing links diagram and gripper footage conceptually; facility identity and one product’s complete handling are not traced.
Deployment ease, cost, customer use and adaptation are unverified claims. Robot close-ups do not establish a complete autonomous packing cycle or installation speed.
The conveyor-to-box example is more specific than the broad repetitive-work slogan.
Show adaptation in the same workstation.
categories.experiment: Start with a real existing conveyor, show placement/setup of the robot and follow one product into its box without changing scenes.
